'''Duncan Austin Lawson''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|MBE|CMath|FIMA|NTF}} is a British [[mathematician]] known for work in mathematics education including university-wide mathematics and statistics support.

==Early life and education==

Lawson attended [[Bury Grammar School]] and later obtained a [[Bachelor's degree|BA]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|D.Phil.]] from the [[University of Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Duncan Lawson MBE |url=https://uk.linkedin.com/in/duncan-lawson-mbe-0a5a57a6 |website=LinkedIn |access-date=8 August 2021}}</ref>

==Career==

Lawson worked for [[British Gas plc]] before moving to [[Coventry University]] in 1987.  His research interests are in efficient computational methods for the calculation of thermal [[radiative heat transfer]].

From 2005 to 2010 Lawson with [[Tony Croft]] established the [[sigma Centre for Excellence in University-wide mathematics and statistics support]], which was awarded the 2011 ''Times Higher Education'' Award for Outstanding Support for Students.<ref>{{cite web |title=THE Awards 2011 |url=https://www.the-awards.co.uk/2021/en/page/archive-2011 |publisher=Times Higher Education |access-date=8 August 2021}}</ref> The centre later developed under the National HE [[STEM]] Programme into the [[sigma Network for Excellence in Mathematics and Statistics Support]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The sigma Network |url=http://www.sigma-network.ac.uk/about/the-sigma-network/ |access-date=8 August 2021}}</ref><ref name="imagoldmedalcitation">{{cite web |title=Citation for two IMA Gold Medals 2016 |date=14 September 2016 |url=https://ima.org.uk/3144/citation-two-ima-gold-medals-2016/ |publisher=Institute of Mathematics and its Applications |access-date=8 August 2021}}</ref>

Lawson was awarded [[National Teaching Fellowship]] in 2005.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Duncan Lawson |url=https://www.advance-he.ac.uk/ntfs/professor-duncan-lawson |publisher=Advance HE |access-date=8 August 2021}}</ref> Lawson also acted as Assistant Chief Executive of the [[Higher Education Academy]] from 2012-13.

Lawson was professor and associate dean of the faculty of science and engineering at [[Coventry University]] (2002–13), director of the [[Maths, Stats & OR Network]] of the [[Higher Education Academy]] (2005-9), and chair of the executive group of the [[More Maths Grads]] project (2008–10).

From 2013-18, Lawson was pro-vice-chancellor of formative education at [[Newman University, Birmingham|Newman University]] in [[Birmingham]], before returning to Coventry.<ref name="NU">{{cite web |title=Mathematics support adds up to an MBE for leading academic |url=https://www.newman.ac.uk/news/mathematics-support-adds-up-to-an-mbe-for-leading-academic/ |publisher=[[Newman University, Birmingham|Newman University]] |accessdate=10 June 2019 |date=8 June 2019}}</ref>

Lawson received the [[Institute of Mathematics and its Applications]]' Gold Medal in 2016 jointly with Croft for "an outstanding contribution to the improvement of the teaching of mathematics" by establishing Sigma.<ref name="imagoldmedalcitation"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Newman University professor awarded prestigious mathematics prize |date=23 July 2016 |url=https://www.indcatholicnews.com/news/30569 |publisher=Independent Catholic News |access-date=8 August 2021}}</ref>

Lawson was appointed [[Member of the Order of the British Empire]] (MBE) in the [[2019 Birthday Honours]] for services to mathematics in higher education.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=62666|supp=y|page=B19|date=8 June 2019}}</ref>

Lawson is currently director of the sigma maths support centre at Coventry University.<ref>{{cite web |title=Contact Our Team |url=http://sigma.coventry.ac.uk/contact-us |website=Coventry University - sigma Mathematics and Statistics Support |access-date=8 August 2021}}</ref>
